races.name: Coolmore Stud St Mark's Basilica Irish EBF Maiden
Moloney's Bar And Music Venue Maiden

runners_data.name: Ard Ri Na Heireann
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with a tendency to fade in the finish, 112 days off, and Jessica O'Gorman (7lb claimer) takes the ride — limited history (one run, 15th over 16f on good) suggests this trip is shorter but the layoff and fade flag are concerns.|

runners_data.name: Desert Swing
runners_data.note: Hold-up type that has faded on its one run (9th over 8f on good), 21 days since running — Robbie Colgan gives it a competent pilot but the style and finishing trend make it hard to place in any scenario.|

runners_data.name: Zarenakarena
runners_data.note: Hold-up style, fades in the finish, ninth on sole start over 8f on good — Jamie Powell is a capable claimer but the distance step-up to 10f is the key unknown and the fade tendency is not encouraging in a controlled-pace race.|

runners_data.name: Giordano
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old (one run, 9th over 10f on good) with an unknown style tag — Ronan Whelan is an excellent jockey and can compensate for inexperience, but the modest debut form makes improvement the only route to relevance.|

runners_data.name: Handani
runners_data.note: Two placed runs on identical good ground (9f and 8f at the Curragh), prominent style, and D K Weld in-form at 2/18 over 14 days; Chris Hayes can slot in second or third and this horse has already shown it knows how to finish.|

runners_data.name: Let's Smash It
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the race; OR 83 is the lowest in the field by some distance and carrying 134lbs, but Ben Coen gets a golden opportunity to dictate an uncontested gallop — the key question is whether the horse has the class to hold on once the prominent group arrives.|

runners_data.name: Lord Darragh
runners_data.note: Placed (2nd) over 10f good at the Curragh last time, ran 10 days ago which is a tight turnaround but Rory Devine has one winner in five over the period — prominent style suits this pace shape ideally and Luke McAteer is capable.|

runners_data.name: Montevetro
runners_data.note: Two placed runs on Standard ground (2nd and 3rd over 10f), 151 days off the track — Seamie Heffernan is a top-class pilot and Denis Hogan sends horses fit after breaks, but the switch from Tapeta to good turf after a long absence is a clear flag.|

runners_data.name: Royal Ballet Blue
runners_data.note: Debutant with no going data and unknown style — Adam Caffrey rides for Jack Foley; entirely unexposed and must be respected on debut if it is well prepared, but zero evidence on which to build a case.|

runners_data.name: The Austrian
runners_data.note: One run (7th over 10f on good), 82 days since, lightly raced — Shane Foley for Mrs John Harrington is a potent combination and the yard handles improvers well; this trip and going are familiar from debut, making improvement plausible.|

runners_data.name: Will You Stop
runners_data.note: Consistent course performer with form over 10f and 12f on good at the Curragh — four runs on similar going producing a place — trained and ridden by Andrew Slattery who knows this horse intimately; prominent style fits.|

runners_data.name: Acula
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's representative (11 winners from 66 in 14 days) with Dylan Browne McMonagle aboard — placed fourth on good over 8f last time; a natural hold-up horse whose true style means it will likely race further back than shown on the map, which mildly constrains its chance in a controlled-pace shape.|

runners_data.name: Saxony Charms
runners_data.note: Two runs over 10f on good ground, placed (3rd) on second try, and headgear has been applied (hg:p) suggesting the trainer expects a step forward; W J Lee has the experience to exploit a prominent position if the pace is honest.|

runners_data.name: Sunatia
runners_data.note: Second over 9f on good at the Curragh on latest start, prominent style, and D K Weld using Leigh Roche — the 14/8f run on soft gives a going concern only if conditions ease, but good ground here suits.|

races.paceDynamic: Let's Smash It is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner maiden and, with no genuine rival to apply early pressure, Ben Coen can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on good ground over 1m2f at the Curragh. The prominent contingent — Handani, Lord Darragh, Will You Stop, and Saxony Charms — will press forward to track but none is likely to force the pace into a true test, meaning the tempo will be honest rather than fierce. Acula is a genuine hold-up type redistributed to the midfield on the map because the rear end of this field is oversubscribed with closers; Dylan Browne McMonagle will likely find Acula racing further back than the map suggests, which constrains its chance in a shape that does not generate a strong late sectional. This race shape — a controlled front-runner setting a sustainable pace with a compact prominent group — strongly favours prominent-to-lead profiles that can travel kindly and quicken in the straight without having burned off energy chasing a hot pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Let's Smash It sets a measured pace and the prominent group tracks comfortably into the straight.
scenarios.body: Let's Smash It dictates a fair gallop and the race assembles itself in a tidy line behind, meaning the horses sitting second to fifth are perfectly positioned to pounce from two furlongs out; on good ground at the Curragh this shape is a classic prominent-runner's race. Handani and Lord Darragh, both with placed form on identical good ground at this trip range, are ideally suited and their jockeys (Hayes, McAteer) have the experience to time the challenge from a tracking position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Midfield Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Let's Smash It goes too hard early and ties up in the final furlong, opening the race to midfield runners.
scenarios.body: A modest OR-83 front-runner carrying 134lbs over 1m2f on good ground could simply run out of fuel if it overcooks the early fractions under pressure from prominent rivals, creating a vacuum that suckers in the midfield; the straight at the Curragh is long enough for a well-timed run to land. Montevetro, with strong placed form over 10f on Standard and a patient Seamie Heffernan in the plate, is the profile that benefits most from a collapsing pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Group Bunches, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types jostle for position early and create a messy, uneven pace through the first half.
scenarios.body: In a 14-runner maiden with four genuine prominent types fighting for the same ground, traffic and interference can disrupt rhythm and produce an uneven tempo that plays into the hands of a horse with tactical versatility; Will You Stop has solid course-and-distance form (3rd and 4th over 10-12f on good at the Curragh) and Andrew Slattery knows his own horse intimately. Saxony Charms, with headgear pointers and two placed runs over 10f on good, also has the gears to exploit a fractured pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Type Improves
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unexposed three-year-olds with limited form shows sharp improvement on its previous run.
scenarios.body: Royal Ballet Blue is a debutant with unknown going profile, while The Austrian and Giordano have shown modest form but carry the potential of lightly-raced sorts trained by shrewd handlers; a significant step forward from any of these on first or second time at this trip could produce a winner that the market has underestimated. The Austrian, handled by Mrs John Harrington with Shane Foley in the saddle, is the most plausible beneficiary given the stable's record with improvers.

watchPoints.text: Let's Smash It sets the entire pace map — if Ben Coen is unable to find the lead cleanly at the start, the race loses its only confirmed front-runner and the tempo becomes unpredictable with the prominent group potentially bunching.|

Acula's redistribution to midfield on the map should be noted: Dylan Browne McMonagle will almost certainly have this hold-up type racing further back than shown, and if the pace is moderate, a late run from the rear may simply not be enough on this track.|

Handani and Sunatia are both from the D K Weld yard — watch for any tactical instructions that see one of them ridden more conservatively as a second string, as the stable runs both in the same race with two different jockeys.|

Royal Ballet Blue is a debutant with no going profile recorded — any market move in the morning should be treated seriously given the absence of public form and the often-shrewd Jack Foley stable with unexposed types.|

The Austrian has had 82 days off since a modest debut seventh, but Mrs John Harrington and Shane Foley rarely appear in maidens without purpose — monitor the market for signs of stable confidence on what would be a significant step forward.|

races.name: Mitsubishi Electric Handicap

runners_data.name: Keke
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse at 6f who has course form here and won at Good going last time out 8 days ago; trainer Lynam is 0/5 in the 14-day window which is a mild negative, but the fitness edge is real — needs a strongly-run race to unleash finishing speed.
runners_data.comment: Keke shaped with promise on his last two starts, and his win three starts back shows he knows how to find the line; distance and going hold no fears, and rated 104 he heads the field on figures. A quick eight-day turnaround is the only mild query, but he arrives fit and primed.

runners_data.name: Howd'yadoit
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type with a win at 5f Good going on a mark of 95; connections Lynam/Kearney represent a lively combo but the step up to 6f on a horse that has struggled to replicate its best over that trip is a genuine concern.
runners_data.comment: Howd'yadoit won five starts back and has since shown enough form — fourth three starts back — to suggest he retains ability, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour at 133 lb from stall seven; the main risk is his latest unplaced effort.

runners_data.name: Chicago Pope
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Murtagh/Coen who won twice at 6f on Good, loves this type of going (6/8 sim-going), and the 70-day break is acceptable given the trainer's positive strike-rate; ideal profile for tracking the front-runner and attacking in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Chicago Pope brings solid recent form to the table — a winner two starts back and a close second three starts back — and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with a 6 lb pull between his official mark and our rating suggesting he's well treated; the main concern is a 70-day absence.

runners_data.name: Bear On The Run
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter, returning after 372 days off for a lightly-raced three-year-old; McMonagle's ability to conserve energy over six furlongs could be the key weapon, and the Curragh 6f suits a horse who won over this course and distance at Leopardstown on Standard.
runners_data.comment: Returning from a 372-day absence is the significant concern here, and she is ranked well below the field on our figures, though the recent win and experience over today's trip and going offer slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Genesis
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent-style performer who has run at least 14 times on similar going with two wins and six places; fits perfectly in the stalking role behind Bear On The Run but does most of his damage at 5f so the extra furlong is a genuine stamina question today.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out suggests Genesis is in decent nick after 13 days, and he has run over today's trip and going before, but a sixth two starts back and unplaced efforts in recent starts hint he can blow hot and cold from stall 8 off 124 lb.

runners_data.name: Go Athletico
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up horse who found 6f on Good ground congenial last time (5th) and has multiple placed efforts; trainer McGuinness is in a very active window (4 runners in 23 days) suggesting the horse is fit, though the age factor and hold-up style mean everything depends on getting a clear run late.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Go Athletico nonetheless showed a second two runs back to hint at better, and has experience of today's distance and going; carrying 122 lb from stall three, he looks a mid-divisional runner at best here.

runners_data.name: Gavoo
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up racer with a tidy recent record (two seconds, a third in last four at 6f Good), carrying 120lbs on a mark of 82; Slattery/Marnane is a sharp combination and the form profile suggests a progressive type who could emerge as a prominent threat if the pace develops in his favour.
runners_data.comment: Gavoo has shown consistent placing ability in recent starts, finishing third last time out and a second three starts back, and he has experience of both today's trip and conditions; the main concern is that he remains yet to score in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Moltophino
runners_data.note: Chronically struggles to get competitive — form reads 9-9-7-9-20 — and while genuinely a hold-up type by style, has been mapped to midfield because of redistribution; the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 reinforces that even a better tactical slot is unlikely to unlock better form here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Moltophino has nonetheless shown experience over today's trip and going, and 19 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; however, a string of ninth-place finishes makes improvement hard to fancy at a competitive weight of 120 lb from stall ten.

runners_data.name: Rock Iguana
runners_data.note: Prominent-style horse who has been competing mainly at 7f and has only 2/8 sim-going strikes; today's 6f on Good is a shorter, faster test and the 10-pound claimer (Huggan) taking the ride means there is a significant experience deficit at a track like the Curragh.
runners_data.comment: Rock Iguana has been winless in his last five starts, with a string of sixths the chief concern, though a second three starts back offers a crumb of encouragement; he returns on a quick turnaround with experience over today's trip and going, but ranked ninth of twelve on our figures he faces a stiff task.

runners_data.name: Finika
runners_data.note: Won impressively at 6f Good last time out and is a natural hold-up runner whose true finishing style has been pushed forward on the map due to redistribution; John James Feane's filly is 13 days fresh and the 4/4 sim-going strike-rate is encouraging — the style compromise is the key caveat to her chance.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and with two unplaced efforts in her last four starts including most recently, Finika is hard to fancy despite a win two starts back and third three starts back suggesting she can find form, and she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Gotta Catch'em All
runners_data.note: In the form of her life with two consecutive wins at 6f Good, but is a deep hold-up horse by inclination who has been redistributed to midfield on the map; the strong recent form (696112) is the headline and if she finds the gaps in a potentially messy finish, the Rutledge/Rogers combination could be live.
runners_data.comment: Ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, Gotta Catch'em All is hard to fancy at these weights, but he does arrive in fair nick — a winner two starts back and a runner-up last time out — with experience of today's distance and going and a decent 19-day gap since his last outing.

runners_data.name: Jon Riggens
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran with a 76-day absence, primarily a hold-up runner who has been mapped to midfield because of redistribution; best form is on Good ground at 6f but recent efforts have been modest and the layoff plus STYLE_FIT flag of 0.91 make it hard to place him competitively in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out to get his head in front for the first time in recent starts, but 76 days off the track is a fitness query and his record over this trip and ground offers experience rather than any established dominance, making him a watch-and-see proposition from stall nine.

races.paceDynamic: Bear On The Run is the one confirmed front-runner in this field and, having been off the track for 372 days, will likely be ridden conservatively to dictate on his own terms rather than pressured into a suicidal gallop — the pace will be honest but controlled, creating a single-file, tempo-managed contest rather than a war up front. Chicago Pope and Genesis are the natural prominent horses who will look to track Bear On The Run closely through the first two furlongs, ensuring there is no false dawdle but also no explosive speed surge. The hold-up brigade — Keke, Howd'yadoit, Go Athletico, and Gavoo — will be hunting for momentum off that steady early fractions, but with the pace neither scorching nor falsely slow, they need a genuinely strong gallop to close from the rear in six furlongs. Several horses tagged as redistributed (Finika, Moltophino, Jon Riggens, Gotta Catch'em All) are true hold-up runners forced into a midfield map position because this field contains more horses wanting to race off the pace than the race shape can comfortably accommodate at the rear. The race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit just off the lone front-runner and pounce entering the final two furlongs, as the controlled early pace will not burn off hold-up horses completely but will reward those with tactical positioning over those forced wide or deep in the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Bear On The Run sets a controlled but honest pace and Chicago Pope or Genesis track him in second or third, enabling a well-timed challenge from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: With a sustainable gallop set by a lone front-runner returning from a lengthy absence, those sat just behind on the bridle get first run at the straight and can repel hold-up horses who need more tempo to close ground on 6f.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Bear On The Run is allowed to dictate completely unchallenged and the hold-up horses find insufficient tempo to close down in the straight.
scenarios.body: A year off the track could mean Daniel James Murphy sends Bear On The Run out with controlled energy and, with no real pace pressure, he could simply lob along and kick clear; Dylan Browne McMonagle is exactly the jockey who can manage such a ride with authority.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens more than expected in the final three furlongs and the genuine hold-up horses find the run of the race from a deep position.
scenarios.body: Keke has course-and-distance form and natural finishing speed, while Howd'yadoit has won off this mark before; both need a strong-enough gallop to make their late runs meaningful over only six furlongs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Shuffle Through
scenarios.trigger: If the race becomes congested mid-pack and a redistributed hold-up type manages to thread through for an unlikely prominent challenge.
scenarios.body: Horses like Gotta Catch'em All, who is in career-best form having won twice recently, could benefit if gaps open late, though their natural trailing style is compromised by being mapped ahead of their comfort zone.

watchPoints.text: Bear On The Run's returning fitness is the pivotal unknown — if his 372-day absence means he ties up in the final furlong, the race opens dramatically for Chicago Pope and Genesis who are poised just behind.

Finika and Gotta Catch'em All are both in excellent recent form but their natural hold-up style is compromised by redistribution to midfield — watch whether Ryan and Rutledge push forward early or drop in regardless, as that decision will define their chance.

Chicago Pope has a 70-day break but Ben Coen on a Murtagh-trained horse returning fresh at the Curragh over a trip the horse has won twice on is a combination that demands respect — watch for an aggressive early move to take the prominent berth.

Genesis drops in trip from recent 5f outings to 6f today — the stamina question over the longer distance at a pace likely to be honest rather than slow is worth monitoring, especially if Bear On The Run bowls along and the early fractions are quicker than Genesis wants.

Rock Iguana's jockey Jared Huggan is a 10-pound claimer operating at a venue and trip with limited relevant course form (2/8 sim-going) — watch for positional errors early if the field compresses behind the front-runner heading into the straight.

races.name: Alpha Centauri Debutante Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Alpha
runners_data.note: Two wins at seven furlongs on good ground at Curragh is a highly specific form match for today; Lordan and Aidan O'Brien have the race-reading ability to make her uncontested lead stick, and her sim-going record of two wins from three on similar conditions is the standout data point in this field.
runners_data.comment: Alpha arrives in red-hot form, winning two of her last three starts including back-to-back victories, and she has experience over today's trip and conditions; the main risk is that our rating of 87 leaves her with something to find.

runners_data.name: Blonde Over Blue
runners_data.note: Her sole win came on soft over seven furlongs with Chris Hayes, who retains the ride, making the jockey continuity a positive, but today's good ground is a step up in going firmness from her winning condition and she has yet to win on a surface this quick.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of five on our figures and her speed rating of 75 gives little encouragement, though she does arrive on the back of a win two starts back and has experience over today's trip and conditions, so she isn't entirely without hope.

runners_data.name: Dancing Destiny
runners_data.note: Has a strong all-round record — five runs producing two wins and two placings on good ground — and her form figures across varying trips show adaptability, but her natural prominent racing style has been mapped toward the rear due to the field's composition, meaning she may not get the forward position her best efforts have come from.
runners_data.comment: Dancing Destiny arrives in fine fettle after winning two starts back and filling the runner-up spot last time out, with experience over today's trip and conditions lending her a solid each-way profile at 128 lb from stall three; the main concern is that our rating of 86 leaves her potentially vulnerable to the top-rated runner.

runners_data.name: Green Empress
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with just two career runs, both placings on good ground at six furlongs, so the step up to seven is an open question; McMonagle is the right booking to help her settle, but the unknown style and trip make her impossible to read with confidence.
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in her last two starts, Green Empress has run over today's trip and going and arrives fresh after 56 days off; winless in recent starts, but her rating heads the field and she looks the one to beat from stall one.

runners_data.name: Ibelieveicanfly
runners_data.note: Her most recent win came over this exact course and trip on good ground just 13 days ago, making her the freshest-form prominent runner in the race; she wears hood headgear and Ronan Whelan rides, and her record of three placings or better from four runs on similar going suggests she handles these conditions well.
runners_data.comment: Ibelieveicanfly was a winner last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving her a solid all-round profile at 128 lb from stall five; the main risk is that her consistency has wavered, with a fourth two starts back.

races.paceDynamic: Alpha is the sole confirmed front-runner in a five-runner field and will stride to the front unchallenged from the outset, setting what is expected to be a sustainable, controlled gallop over Curragh's seven furlongs on good ground. Blonde Over Blue and Ibelieveicanfly are both prominent types who will track Alpha closely through the early stages, but neither has the profile to fire up a pace battle, meaning Alpha dictates tempo entirely on her own terms. Dancing Destiny, a natural prominent racer nudged back on the map due to the field's positional balance, and the unknown Green Empress will race in the rear half, but this is not a true hold-up field — there are more pace-committed types than genuine closers. The race shape overwhelmingly favours an uncontested front-runner allowed to travel sweetly and kick from the front, making prominent-to-lead profiles the clear tactical beneficiaries on this going.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Alpha Controls, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Alpha settles comfortably in front and Lordan times his quickening run from two furlongs out without being pressured through the race.
scenarios.body: Alpha dictates a measured pace, turns the race into a test of class and resolution from the front, and her two wins on good going at this trip underline the suitability of conditions. Prominent types tracking her closely have the shortest route to challenging, but without a pace injection from rivals, a front-runner who travels well has every advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If Alpha sets a genuinely moderate pace that produces a sprint finish and the prominent trackers have more gas in reserve.
scenarios.body: Ibelieveicanfly, whose most recent win came over this exact trip at Curragh on good going, is ideally placed to pounce if the race slows and turns tactical, while Blonde Over Blue's single win also came on soft at seven furlongs showing the trip is within range. A messy, bunched finish from a crawl suits horses racing just off the pace with a finishing kick.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Rush From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If a genuinely slow early tempo creates a sprint that benefits the horses furthest back, and Green Empress's unknown style maps to hold-up.
scenarios.body: Green Empress has placed in both career starts on good ground at six furlongs and stepping up to seven is the key unknown, but if her style proves to be hold-up she arrives with momentum in a sprint finish. Dancing Destiny's versatile form across five placed or winning efforts on good ground gives her the tactical experience to pick off tired rivals late, though neither is a true closer.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Upsets
scenarios.trigger: If Alpha goes off too fast for the conditions, burns through her rivals, and stops abruptly in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: This requires Alpha to misjudge her own tempo, which is a low-probability outcome given Lordan's experience and the horse's settled front-running profile over this course and trip. Should it materialise, the two Joseph O'Brien-trained runners tracking closely — Blonde Over Blue and Dancing Destiny — are best placed to collect the pieces.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Ibelieveicanfly attempts to press Alpha for the lead from the gates — if she does, it converts this from a solo-leader race into a contested gallop that changes the entire shape.

Green Empress is 56 days off the track and steps up in trip for the first time; if she shows signs of greenness or fails to travel, her chance evaporates quickly in a five-runner field with no pace to hide in.

Dancing Destiny's redistribution to the rear of the map is artificial — if she instinctively pushes forward into her natural prominent position, the pace dynamic could compress and favour closers more than the current shape suggests.

The going is a consistent Good across all distances at Curragh today, meaning no surface variance to exploit — horses with proven good-ground form hold a clear edge over those relying on easier conditions for their best performances.

races.name: Coolmore Stud City Of Troy Tom Cooper Irish EBF Futurity Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: City of Dubai
runners_data.note: Rated 120 and two-from-two under W J Lee for Pat Twomey, winning last on Good over 8f, so dropping to 7f is a question mark — a natural prominent racer whose map position at hold-up understates how forward he is likely to travel in practice; 15 days between runs is fresh enough.
runners_data.comment: Beaten only a neck on his latest start, with a win the run before that, City of Dubai arrives in cracking recent form and has experience of today's trip and conditions; the concern is whether 131 lb from stall 6 blunts his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Florida Bay
runners_data.note: Four runs of experience including two wins for Aidan O'Brien, with Ronan Whelan aboard and a solid record on Good going (4/4 sim-going), but this is a horse that wants to be up in the action — nudged back to a midfield map slot purely because of the prominent traffic ahead of it in this field.
runners_data.comment: Florida Bay arrives on the back of a win last time out and a winner three starts back, showing a knack for getting his head in front, and he has run over today's trip and going before; the main risk is that our rating of 90 leaves him something to find with the top-rated runner.

runners_data.name: Giant Sequoia
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's second string who won over this exact 7f Curragh trip on Good going last time; Wayne Lordan knows the track and 56 days off the track is the main query, though the horse's profile — prominent, experienced at the distance — fits this race shape as well as any runner here.
runners_data.comment: Giant Sequoia won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving him solid claims on conditions; the main risk is a 56-day absence since that victory, and 131 lb from stall one will demand a forward showing.

runners_data.name: Green Dreamer
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's progressive 2yo who most recently won over 8f on Good going; stepped back to 7f asks whether his stamina advantage is removed, but Declan McDonogh riding a prominent-style horse over a flat track with honest pace suits his in-running style.
runners_data.comment: Green Dreamer won last time out but ranks fifth of six on our figures, with a speed rating of 54 doing little to inspire confidence; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 30 days between runs leaves fitness mildly in question.

runners_data.name: Nail House
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner under Dylan Browne McMonagle, won over 6f Good going last time, so the step up to 7f is the key test — if he gets into a duel with Nola Soul, the extra furlong may find him out, but Joseph Patrick O'Brien's barn is in strong form (11/66 T14) and he will ensure maximum early use is made of his pace.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Nail House faces a stiff ask against stronger company, though he does arrive on the back of a win two starts back and a third last time out, with experience over today's trip and going at least offering some grounding.

runners_data.name: Nola Soul
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in two starts, both at 7f on Good going at Curragh, and trained by J A Stack who has a quieter book (0/9 T14) — 65 days off the track is the longest absence in this field but Seamie Heffernan's booking for the only unbeaten horse in the race is a clear positive.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins make Nola Soul the one to beat here, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions to call upon; the 65-day absence is the only query, though he tops our ratings on the form provided.

races.paceDynamic: Nola Soul and Nail House are confirmed front-runners and will fight for early supremacy over the opening two furlongs of this 7f Curragh contest, creating a genuinely contested gallop that should be honest rather than manic on good ground. Giant Sequoia, Green Dreamer, and City of Dubai are all natural prominent-racers who will track close to the pace, leaving Florida Bay — also a natural prominent type — shuffled back further than ideal given the volume of forward-going horses. The field holds more prominent types than can all secure their natural position, with Nola Soul and Nail House most likely to actually lead, and Giant Sequoia and Green Dreamer best placed to fill the true prominent berths behind them. A competitive, even gallop on a flat track with six runners strongly favours horses capable of travelling prominently and sustaining their effort through the final two furlongs — hold-up tactics are structurally disadvantaged here because there will be no slow early phase to exploit and no congestion to weave through.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Nola Soul and Nail House push each other along and the gallop is honest from the outset, setting up a strongly run race.
scenarios.body: The pace duel softens both leaders late, and a horse travelling prominently just off the lead — without expending energy in the battle — picks up most cleanly in the final furlong. Good ground at Curragh 7f rewards horses with a high cruising speed who can switch off slightly before asserting.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Dictates, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Nola Soul (two wins, unbeaten) is allowed to stride clear without a serious early duel and controls tempo to suit herself.
scenarios.body: The pace is comfortable enough that the leader preserves energy for the closing stages, and Nola Soul's unbeaten two-from-two record over this course and trip at Good going becomes the decisive factor. The prominent chasers cannot close the gap on a horse that has never been headed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Blows Leaders Out
scenarios.trigger: If the early duel between Nola Soul and Nail House is more intense than expected, burning both off turning for home.
scenarios.body: A horse that has been restrained fractionally off the boil — such as Florida Bay, who has won at this trip and is trained by Aidan O'Brien — gets cover and produces a sustained late run as the front pair fade. Florida Bay's redistribution to midfield is a concern given its natural prominence, but it has the class record to capitalise if the race falls apart.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Class Edge, Quiet Day
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is surprisingly moderate and the race turns into a sprint from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A high-OR prominent horse with tactical speed exploits the compressed pace and sprints clear before rivals can react; City of Dubai's OR of 120 and two-from-two form over 8f suggests class superiority even if the trip is a slight unknown. However this scenario depends on a shape that contradicts the two front-runners' profiles and is the least likely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Nail House or Nola Soul blinks first in the opening two furlongs — if one tries to dominate outright rather than share the lead, the race shape changes decisively around both of them.
Giant Sequoia is 56 days off the track; watch the market move in the hour before post — any significant support would suggest stable confidence that the layoff is irrelevant.

Florida Bay is a natural prominent type buried in midfield by this race's pace volume — if Ronan Whelan cannot find a forward berth in the early strides, the horse will race outside its comfort zone and its chance shrinks accordingly.

Green Dreamer drops back from 8f to 7f for the first time since winning at that trip — watch whether McDonogh positions him prominently or allows him to fill the role of a pace-follower, as the latter suits his profile in this shape.

City of Dubai, also stepping back to 7f after two wins over 8f, will be worth monitoring for how aggressively W J Lee tries to hold a forward berth given the number of pace rivals; if he is forced wider or back, his chance is reduced.

races.name: Neville O'Byrne Memorial Irish EBF Fillies Handicap

runners_data.name: Marazion
runners_data.note: Won over 1m2f on Good and placed at 1m4f in the same conditions; Shane Foley in the saddle for Harrington, but 55 days off and six-runner form of 7-1-2-6-6 suggests inconsistency — needs a clean early lead to be at her best.
runners_data.comment: Marazion showed her class when winning and running second in recent starts, and has experience of today's trip and conditions. Carrying 140 lb after 55 days off is a query, but her rating of 95 marks her as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Denim And Diamonds
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien filly returning after 61 days with tongue-tie noted; best recent run was a fourth over 1m1f on Good and hold-up style suits the scenario where the pace destroys the front-runners, but her form figures of 80-784 point to frustrating inconsistency.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and without a run for 61 days, Denim And Diamonds nonetheless holds strong claims here on a rating of 92 — ranked third among the 12 runners — and she has experience over today's distance and going, though recapturing her best form after that layoff is the key question.

runners_data.name: Navy Waters
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with eight runs over 1m2f-plus on Good — her best ground — and comes in fresh on just 10 days' turnaround; the tongue-tie is retained and W J Lee knows this mare, making her one of the more reliable profiles in the field for a genuine-pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Navy Waters has shown consistent placing ability, finishing third in two of her last five starts, and returns on a quick ten-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and conditions in her favour; the concern is she remains winless in recent starts and must prove she can convert her solid efforts into something more decisive.

runners_data.name: Beauparc
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up type who showed a big effort when second over 1m1f on Good recently; Jack Kearney (3lb claimer) takes off some weight but the form prior to that placed run has been modest and she needs the pace to truly collapse to get involved.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Beauparc does bring distance and going experience to the table and was a second two starts back, though her latest effort was unplaced; carrying 130 lb looks a stiff ask as she tries to bounce back.

runners_data.name: Railwayview Lady
runners_data.note: Placed second over 1m1f on Good last year but more recently posted 8-9-8-16 in similar or better company; runs from a hold-up position and needs the stars to align with a strong pace and a clear run, which is not guaranteed in a 12-runner field from her rearward berth.
runners_data.comment: Railwayview Lady has run over today's trip and going, and with her trainer firing at 29% over the past fortnight, conditions look to suit — our rating of 88 marks her as a serious threat in this field; the concern is a sequence of three poor runs in recent starts, and 55 days off since.

runners_data.name: Yousaynothingatall
runners_data.note: Front-runner for Joseph O'Brien ridden by Dylan Browne McMonagle; has recent form of 3-3-1-3-2 which looks solid, but racing against three other pace-hungry types over 1m4f may mean she burns her stamina fighting for position rather than setting a comfortable tempo.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out and a winner three starts back, Yousaynothingatall arrives with experience over today's trip and going, though carrying 130 lb looks the chief obstacle to adding another success here.

runners_data.name: Vanir
runners_data.note: Ben Coen partner for J P Murtagh, three-year-old with a sharp 4/4 Good-ground profile including a win over 1m2f on Good; progressive and prominent in style, she is well-treated relative to rivals and her course form over similar distances is the most reliable recent dataset in this race.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out after winning two starts back, Vanir arrives on 35 days off with experience of today's trip and conditions; the drop to a speed rating of 74 and a rating ranked seventh of twelve suggest she faces a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Nellcote
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced three-year-old with just two runs, winning over 1m2f on Good and fourth over 1m on Good; a genuine front-runner who goes well fresh, but stepping into a 12-runner handicap from a small-field maiden win brings significant unknowns around traffic and pace management.
runners_data.comment: Rated well below her rivals on our figures and ranked last of the 12 runners, Nellcote is hard to fancy at the weights despite winning last time out; she has run over today's trip and going before, but a 42-day absence adds to the query marks.

runners_data.name: Letiza
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery's six-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by style, but with several hold-up types vying for the rear of the field her race is most likely to be run from further forward than she'd prefer — her STYLE_FIT score of 0.93 reflects that racing out of role tempers her realistic chance regardless of the pace shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, Letiza is hard to fancy, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a reasonable 19-day break.

runners_data.name: Killyclogher Rose
runners_data.note: Won over 1m1f on Good and has placed at 1m2f on Standard; goes forward under Wayne Lordan and has the form to compete in this company on paper, but is one of four confirmed pace types and her chance may be compromised if a pace war develops rather than a controlled lead.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down our assessments and with a speed rating of 65 that makes her hard to fancy, Killyclogher Rose does bring a win two starts back and experience over today's trip and going, but the latest sixth leaves her needing significant improvement.

runners_data.name: My Girl Grace
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for G M Lyons ridden by a 7lb claimer; won her maiden over 1m on Soft and has since posted 7-7 in stronger company on Good ground — the step to 1m4f is unproven and the hold-up profile means she needs plenty to go right.
runners_data.comment: Won three starts back but has posted back-to-back sevenths since, leaving her form an open question; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 119 lb is manageable, though her rating of 82 suggests she faces stiffer opposition here.

runners_data.name: Neo Smart
runners_data.note: J S Bolger five-year-old with a prominent style and recent form of 7-7-4-5-4-6; drops back from sprint distances and races rarely beyond 1m in recent history — tongue-tie fitted and the step to 1m4f looks a significant ask on current form and distance profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, Neo Smart faces a stiff ask here; she has run over today's going before and returns on a quick turnaround of just six days, but consistency has been a persistent issue and it is hard to make a case for her at this level.

races.paceDynamic: Marazion, Yousaynothingatall, Nellcote, and Killyclogher Rose all want to be on or near the lead, creating a genuinely contested gallop from the outset over 1m4f on Good ground at the Curragh — stamina will be tested and the fractions are unlikely to be kind to those who press on without reserve. The pace duel between four legitimate front-runners will stretch the field early, meaning the strong pace is not simply predicted but structurally inevitable given how many horses need that position. Letiza is a genuine hold-up type redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear of the field is already packed; her true running style is rearward and her ability to influence the race from an unnatural position should be discounted. This pace shape emphatically favours resolute, well-stamped closers and strong mid-division travellers who can sit off a genuine gallop and pick up the pieces in the final two furlongs — horses like Navy Waters, Vanir, and Denim And Diamonds are best positioned by profile to capitalise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the four-way pace battle burns out the front-runners and the race sets up for a sustained late charge from behind the tempo.
scenarios.body: Marazion, Yousaynothingatall, Nellcote, and Killyclogher Rose fight for position and consume each other's stamina reserves, leaving the race wide open entering the straight; Navy Waters and Vanir, both Good-ground performers with strong recent form, are ideally placed to swoopfrom mid-division with energy in reserve.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pace-Setter Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners — most likely Marazion or Nellcote — establishes clear early control and dictates a measured, sustainable tempo.
scenarios.body: Rather than burning out in a four-way duel, one leader settles into a controlled gallop that plays to their stamina and makes it harder for closers to close the gap; Marazion has the strongest form in this company at this trip and Nellcote's two-run form over 12f-plus on Good is sharp and progressive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves honest but not truly ruinous, and horses racing just off the leaders in the prominent group conserve enough energy to win.
scenarios.body: Vanir in particular has an outstanding Good-ground profile at 1m2f-plus and has shown the ability to race prominently before quickening; a race that burns out the true front-runners but leaves the stalkers with enough fuel suits this profile well, and Navy Waters' course form and consistency at this trip make her a natural player.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Very Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is extreme and the leaders tie up badly inside the final quarter-mile, opening the door for the deepest closers.
scenarios.body: Denim And Diamonds and Railwayview Lady would be the beneficiaries of a truly punishing pace collapse, though both have inconsistent form and the latter has struggled in similar race shapes before; this scenario is the least likely because the genuinely held-up types are scarce and the redistributed Letiza cannot be relied upon to execute from her natural rearward position in this field.

watchPoints.text: Marazion and Yousaynothingatall may clash aggressively for the lead in the first two furlongs — watch for a fierce pace duel that could compromise both horses' stamina before halfway.

Nellcote is lightly raced and steps into a competitive 12-runner handicap for the first time; she may find the pace scenario more turbulent than her small-field maiden form suggests and could be swamped early.

Letiza is a genuine hold-up type running out of role in this field — if she is shuffled back to her natural position rather than the midfield shown on the map, she may need an even more extreme pace collapse than Scenario D requires.

Navy Waters runs on just 10 days' rest with the tongue-tie retained — confirm market confidence at the off, as W J Lee booking for a horse with eight Good-ground runs at this trip suggests connections are primed for this specific race shape.

Vanir's trainer J P Murtagh has only two runners in the 14-day window but this three-year-old's Good-ground record is the cleanest in the field — watch her market move as a possible stable confidence play against older rivals.

races.name: Comer Group International Irish St. Leger Trial Stakes

runners_data.name: Carmers
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a smart win over 2m (16f) on Good ground and consistent form at this trip; the 65-day break is worth noting but trainer Twomey keeps horses fit, and the Good ground suits — well placed to capitalise off a strong pace.
runners_data.comment: Carmers won two starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a clear threat at the head of the ratings, though a run of 65 days off the track is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Dallas Star
runners_data.note: Wants to lead but has managed just zero wins from 15 starts on similar going, and the 10-day turnaround after a poor run is unconvincing; likely to fight for the front and be a casualty of the pace rather than a beneficiary.
runners_data.comment: Dallas Star has run over today's trip and going before, and a placed effort two starts back suggests some ability, yet he remains winless in his last six starts and his recent fifth and seventh hint at inconsistency that makes him hard to trust from the middle of the field.

runners_data.name: Kizlyar
runners_data.note: Two recent wins give him strong form claims, and jockey Dylan Browne McMonagle is a major booking for Joseph O'Brien; races prominently, handles Good ground, and the step up to 1m6f tests stamina but his pedigree and winning thread make him hard to dismiss.
runners_data.comment: Kizlyar has won three of his last five starts, including back-to-back wins, and has experience over today's trip and going, but ranked last of seven on our figures and returning after 67 days off, he makes little appeal at the weights.

runners_data.name: Layfayette
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who has won twice and placed in recent starts, including a win over 2m and a placing over 1m6f; at nine years old he remains consistent and this strong-pace scenario is precisely what he needs to produce his best late run.
runners_data.comment: Layfayette won two starts back and was a runner-up three starts back, giving him an encouraging recent profile, and he returns fit on 16 days' rest having run over today's trip and going before, with 135 lb the one thing to shoulder.

runners_data.name: Leinster
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner with a win over 1m2f on Good ground last time, but faces direct competition for the lead from Asakir and Dallas Star; if he gets embroiled in a three-way duel he risks burning out before the home straight despite his genuine ability.
runners_data.comment: Leinster has a win among his last five starts and has experience of both today's trip and going, while the 64 days off is the chief concern under 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Queenstown
runners_data.note: 300-day absence is the dominant concern here — he has placed in staying trips consistently but returning from such a long layoff over 1m6f on Good ground is a major ask, even for a horse with solid form figures when fresh.
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in recent starts, Queenstown has run over today's trip and going and shapes as a clear threat at 135 lb with an official rating of 110, yet his 300-day absence is the one question mark he must answer.

runners_data.name: Asakir
runners_data.note: Youngest runner in the field at three and races off 9lbs less weight; has only four runs to his name and this is his first attempt at 1m6f, making stamina an unknown — he wants to front-run but risks burning his limited reserves fighting Leinster and Dallas Star for the lead.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the assessments and returning after 66 days off, Asakir is hard to fancy despite a win and a second in recent starts; he has run over today's trip before, but a seventh last time out leaves plenty to prove.

races.paceDynamic: Leinster, Asakir, and Dallas Star all want to lead, guaranteeing an aggressive, front-loaded gallop over this testing 1m6f trip on Good ground at the Curragh. Leinster has the strongest recent front-running credentials, winning over 1m2f last time, while Asakir and Dallas Star will push him every yard from the off, meaning none of the three can settle and conserve energy as they might prefer. The resulting strong tempo will stretch the field early, burning out those who over-commit and playing directly into the hands of hold-up and prominent types with genuine stamina reserves who can produce a sustained late run on the flat. This race shape firmly favours hold-up and midfield runners with proven staying ability — Layfayette, Carmers, and Queenstown profile best off a strong pace set by horses who may have burned too many matches fighting for the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Leinster, Asakir, and Dallas Star burn each other out fighting for the lead, setting a genuinely strong gallop that cracks the pace-setters before the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The sustained early tempo drains the front-runners before the home straight, opening the race up for those who have settled off the pace and can produce a powerful, relentless late run over the final two furlongs on Good ground. Layfayette (has won twice recently and handles this trip) and Carmers (won over 2m/16f in good form) are ideally placed to swoop, while Queenstown — proven in staying trips — also fits.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Front-Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Leinster or Asakir breaks cleanly and the others back off, allowing a single front-runner to control a sensible, measured gallop rather than a destructive duel.
scenarios.body: A controlled pace would be far kinder to the leader's stamina reserves, potentially allowing them to steal a march turning into the home straight before rivals can close. Leinster, who won over 1m2f and has strong Curragh form, is the likeliest beneficiary if given a soft lead, with Asakir — unexposed at this trip as a 3-year-old — also capable of front-running to victory.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is strong enough to crack the leaders but not slow enough for pure closers to get back into contention, favouring horses travelling prominently just off the front.
scenarios.body: Carmers, who races prominently and has proven form over this distance (won over 2m, placed over 1m6f), could slot in just behind the leader and time a run perfectly, while Kizlyar — prominent in style, with two recent wins and a strong jockey booking in Dylan Browne McMonagle — has the class to pounce.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart Chaotically
scenarios.trigger: If the early three-way duel produces a stop-start, uneven pace rather than a true genuine gallop, creating a tactical mess over 1m6f.
scenarios.body: An uneven tempo would muddle the race shape, potentially suiting a horse like Queenstown — who has a 300-day absence to overcome but has placed consistently in staying trips on Good ground — or Layfayette, whose recent winning form suggests he retains strong ability when conditions stabilise. Both handle the distance but their chances are tempered by the unpredictability of this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Leinster, Asakir, or Dallas Star actually cedes the lead early — if none of them relents, the pace will be so strong that all three are likely to be spent before the final furlong.
Queenstown's 300-day absence makes him a significant watch in the paddock and early in the race — if he shows any signs of ring-rustiness or races ungenerously, he can be discounted immediately.

Kizlyar has had an inconsistent record in his last five runs including poor efforts at Leopardstown (10th) and the Curragh (9th over 1m6f) — his two recent wins were over shorter trips, so watch whether he sees this trip out fully.

Asakir's weight allowance (126lbs vs 135lbs for older rivals) is a meaningful swing over 1m6f on Good ground — if the pace falls apart and becomes tactical, his youth and lighter burden could make him harder to catch than his limited experience suggests.

Layfayette's rider Adam Caffrey is a relatively low-profile booking for a race of this nature — watch whether Caffrey tracks the right horses early, as the hold-up style only works here if he is poised to deliver a run between the 3f and 2f poles.

races.name: Friends Of Moorefield GAA Handicap

runners_data.name: Clonmacash
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with strong recent 6f form at the Curragh on Good ground, five-pound claimer Sam Coen adds value, visor headgear in place, and Adrian McGuinness yard in solid form at 4/23 over 14 days — a natural fit for sitting just off a controlled solo pace.
runners_data.comment: Clonmacash arrives here 19 days after a fifth, yet to win in his last six starts, though a third three starts back shows he can threaten the frame; he has run over today's trip and conditions before, and a mark of 72 leaves our rating of 80 suggesting some headroom, though stall 22 and 142 lb are factors to weigh.

runners_data.name: Mint Man
runners_data.note: True hold-up performer with two wins and five places from 11 runs on Good, ridden by a seven-pound claimer which helps offset the weight, and last-run Curragh win over 6f is the standout piece of form in the race — needs a clear passage from midfield.
runners_data.comment: Mint Man won last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, but a mark of 72 and draw 10 at 142 lb are the counterweights, and his form in recent starts has been patchy beyond that latest success.

runners_data.name: Soulful Diva
runners_data.note: Hold-up three-year-old just six days since her last run, good record on Good going at 5-6f, but dropping back in trip from her recent 6f efforts and trainer sending out just 1/18 in the 14-day window tempers enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Soulful Diva bounced back sharply last time with a second, has run over today's trip and going, and her rating of 80 marks her as a serious threat from stall 25, though consistency remains the key question.

runners_data.name: Bold Optimist
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a solid placed record on Good ground but primarily campaigned over 5f; stepping back up to 6f at the Curragh on a handicap mark that has him carrying 139lbs, Scott McCullagh takes the mount for a yard with no recent winners.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Bold Optimist nonetheless brings a consistent placed thread — third last time out and a second two starts back — and has run over today's trip and going before, though 139 lb from stall 21 are not inconsiderable asks for a gelding rated 69 officially.

runners_data.name: Hugo's Girl
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with four places from seven runs on Good ground at 6f, W J Lee retains the ride, and her consistent finishing suggests she can be competitive if traffic allows — but reliant on finding a gap from her position behind the midfield pack.
runners_data.comment: Placed twice in her last six starts — second last time out and a second four starts back — Hugo's Girl arrives 13 days fresh and has run over today's distance and going before, though she remains winless in recent starts and a hefty 139 lb from stall 26 are the headwinds to weigh.

runners_data.name: Four Blondes
runners_data.note: Hold-up sprinter 31 days off the track with a modest recent form string, no wins or places on Good in five attempts — the step back to 6f after a poor effort over 8f does little to inspire confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Four Blondes returns after 31 days looking better treated than her official mark of 68 suggests, with our rating of 82 offering meaningful leanings her way; fifth last time out and fourth three starts back hint at ability, and she has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Treasured Royal
runners_data.note: Hold-up three-year-old by a trainer firing at 6/24 in the past fortnight, 51 days between runs is the key query, but a win on Good and multiple places at 5-6f suggest the ability is there if Gavin Cromwell has freshened this filly up.
runners_data.comment: Treasured Royal shaped with promise when third three starts back and her trainer is in red-hot form at 29% over the past fortnight, making her a serious threat despite being winless in her last six starts and returning after 51 days off.

runners_data.name: Pinar Del Rio
runners_data.note: Prominent-styled seven-year-old returning from 105 days off the track; has placed three times on Good at 6-7f in his history but the extended absence for a veteran at this level is a significant concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and absent for 105 days, Pinar Del Rio does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a rating of 76 offers some encouragement — though carrying 137 lb from stall 19 gives connections plenty to navigate.

runners_data.name: Poweracclaim
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a tidy placed record across Good-ground 5-6f races, Ben Coen takes the mount for J P Murtagh, and 42 days since last run should mean he is fresh; sits just the right side of the pace for this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Poweracclaim has been knocking on the door, finishing third last time out and fourth two starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going gives him solid claims here; the risk is he remains winless in recent starts and must prove he can convert.

runners_data.name: Chester Nimitz
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with headgear (tongue-tie, blinkers) who has been running over 7-8f recently; dropping to 6f is a positive switch, Shane Foley adds class in the saddle, but a form string reading 99 in recent starts is deeply uninspiring.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Chester Nimitz has run over today's trip and going before, and 19 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; however, a persistent pattern of ninth-place finishes is hard to ignore, and 135 lb from stall 18 adds further pressure.

runners_data.name: Unidos
runners_data.note: Hold-up three-year-old flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — a real concern in a race where the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to compress the field; 45 days off with a yard showing 0/6 in the fortnight compounds the reservations.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 13 of 31, Unidos has experience over today's trip and going but returns after 45 days off carrying 135 lb from stall 20, and his recent string of fifths and unplaced runs offer little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Kiss Don't Tell
runners_data.note: Prominent three-year-old with limited form on Good at 5-6f, five-pound claimer Nicola Burns rides, only four career runs so experience is a question — dropped in trip to 6f but has not shown the form to suggest she is a major force here.
runners_data.comment: Kiss Don't Tell showed a promising second two starts back but was well beaten on her latest outing eight days ago, and winless in her last four starts, she faces a stiff task from stall 30 carrying 134 lb, despite having experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Cladach
runners_data.note: Hold-up three-year-old trained by Joseph Patrick O'Brien who has fired in 11 winners from 66 runners in the past fortnight — Dylan Browne McMonagle on board adds significant jockey quality, but a fade flag and only three career runs over 6-7f on Good leave questions about readiness for a 31-runner handicap.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, Cladach was fourth three starts back but has drifted since, finishing ninth and then unplaced most recently; experience over today's trip and going helps, though his 133 lb burden from stall 23 gives him plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Ocean Echo
runners_data.note: Prominent three-year-old whose trainer Mark Fahey is 0/6 in the past 14 days; has placed at 6-7f on Good before but a form string of 686 in recent starts shows he is knocking on the door without converting.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Ocean Echo at least has experience of today's trip and going to call on, and 29 days between runs suggests he returns fresh; however, a run of two sixths and an eighth in recent outings makes it hard to fancy him from 14th in the rankings.

runners_data.name: Beat The Devil
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer whose natural position is at the back of the field — here mapped to midfield due to the congestion of off-the-pace horses in this race; his recent form over distances up to 18f suggests this 6f trip is far shorter than ideal, and the style fit discount is warranted.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 24 of 31 on our figures, Beat The Devil faces a stiff ask carrying 132 lb from stall 11, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a sharp 13-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Glasarmi
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner — three-year-old with only three career runs and a modest form string of 545, but the uncontested lead on Good ground over 6f is a major positional advantage; Luke McAteer takes the ride for a small stable, and 64 days since last run is worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked well down the field on our figures, Glasarmi is hard to fancy here; she has run over today's trip before and returns after 64 days off, though the 132 lb burden from stall 14 does her no favours.

runners_data.name: Are You In Or Out
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse with a single win from 15 runs on Good ground — his natural racing position is from the rear, but the field's volume of similar types means he cannot get that berth naturally in this race; James Ryan rides and the 42-day break adds uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Beaten into eighth last time out after 42 days off, and her most recent win came four starts back, so she arrives needing to recapture that form; she has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 69 offers encouragement, though a mark of 61 and 131 lb from stall 8 make it competitive.

runners_data.name: Cashel Blue
runners_data.note: Three-year-old whose last three runs include a 5f win on Good and two places at the same trip — naturally inclined to race from the rear, he is one of the hold-up horses most likely to push forward given his tactical speed over short distances, which could make him a factor if he settles close enough.
runners_data.comment: Cashel Blue won three starts back and was third two starts back, so there is upward momentum to consider, but she was only fifth last time out and her 8-day turnaround leaves little time to bounce back; she has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 66 gives her a slim edge over her official mark.

runners_data.name: Coincidental Glory
runners_data.note: Prominent three-year-old trained by Adrian McGuinness alongside Clonmacash, useful placed form on Good at 6-7f, and 26 days between runs is fine — Adam Caffrey rides and the yard's 4/23 form in the past fortnight is encouraging for both runners.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Coincidental Glory does offer some encouragement with a second and third in recent outings, though a ninth last time out is harder to ignore; he has run over today's trip and going before, but 131 lb from stall 12 makes life no easier.

runners_data.name: Absoluteassignment
runners_data.note: A horse whose natural inclination is to race off the pace — mapping him to midfield in this race reflects the overcrowded hold-up group rather than his own preference; a 2nd over 6f on Good is the best piece of form, but Gavin Ryan's booking adds confidence if he can get close enough.
runners_data.comment: Absoluteassignment is yet to win in his last six starts, though a second three starts back offers some encouragement; carrying 130 lb from stall 9 on a comeback of 35 days looks the chief concern, even if he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Caislean Ni Cuan
runners_data.note: Prominent three-year-old with four runs on Good at 6-7f and a best finish of 4th; N G McCullagh takes the ride for Thomas Mullins who has no recent winners from six runs in the past fortnight — limited upside suggested by the form string.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked 23 of 31 on our figures, Caislean Ni Cuan is hard to fancy, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a quick 13-day turnaround fit and ready.

runners_data.name: Battleforsupremacy
runners_data.note: Three-year-old returning from 176 days off the track, a long absence that dominates the note; trains with Daniel McLoughlin who fields three runners here, and while a prior win shows ability, racing in a 31-runner field first time back after nearly six months is a stern ask — natural hold-up style is squeezed out of position by the field's composition.
runners_data.comment: Battleforsupremacy showed a return to form with a third last time out, and a winner four starts back, but 176 days off the track raises fitness questions; he has run over today's trip and going, and carries 129 lb from stall 7.

runners_data.name: Irish Rumour
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up performer with four places from 15 runs on Good and a tendency to finish in the frame without winning — here operating from a position further forward than ideal due to redistribution, which is unlikely to help a horse who relies on a strong gallop developing ahead.
runners_data.comment: Irish Rumour has experience over today's trip and going but has been winless in her last five starts, with her best recent effort a second four starts back; carrying 129 lb from stall 13 makes further progress a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Rosato
runners_data.note: Prominent five-year-old with two wins and three places from 15 Good-ground runs, a 2nd over 6f at the Curragh in his recent history is the key form line; 13 days between runs and Rory Mulligan (5) takes the ride — low ORating of 58 means big weights are not a concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Rosato does bring distance and going experience to the table, and her second two starts back suggests she retains some ability; however, carrying 128 lb from stall 31 gives connections plenty to overcome.

runners_data.name: Caffu Zafeen
runners_data.note: Hold-up five-year-old whose form over Good ground at 5-7f has deteriorated sharply — a string of 000 in recent starts tells a clear story; bumped forward in the map from the rear group, the style fit discount simply adds to an already weak profile.
runners_data.comment: Caffu Zafeen has been consistently below par, unplaced in his last three starts and finishing sixth in the two before that, leaving him winless in his recent five outings; a trainer without a strike from 24 runners in the past fortnight makes him very hard to fancy, despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked last of the field on our figures, Raven's Call faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns after a 36-day break with some freshness to offer from stall 28.

runners_data.name: De Songbird
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 26 of 31 on our figures, De Songbird faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's going before and returns after 39 days, but consistent finishes towards the rear make her hard to fancy from stall 15 carrying 121 lb.

runners_data.name: Fontaine Khaled
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked 25 of 31 on our figures, Fontaine Khaled is hard to fancy, though she did finish third three starts back and has run over today's trip and going before, while 15 days since her last outing suggests she is fit enough.

runners_data.name: Platino Bianco
runners_data.comment: Ranked 28 of 31 on our figures, Platino Bianco faces a stiff ask, with three consecutive finishes of sixth, fifth and fifth in recent starts offering little encouragement; she has run over today's trip and going before, and a winner four starts back at least confirms she can find the line.

runners_data.name: She's On The Ball
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked 29 of 31 on our figures, She's On The Ball faces a stiff task from stall 24 carrying 119 lb, though a third last time out offers a sliver of encouragement and she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Lady Landhort
runners_data.comment: Ranked 30 of 31 on our figures, Lady Landhort's recent form offers little encouragement — unplaced in her last two starts and winless in her last five — though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a quick six-day turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Glasarmi is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 31-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival who will pressure them from the front — this means a controlled, single-file gallop is the most likely race shape from the outset on Good ground over 6f at the Curragh. With Glasarmi able to dictate a sustainable tempo unchallenged, the race will be set up for horses that can track closely in behind and kick off that steady pace, rather than those waiting for a strong gallop to develop from the rear. The pack of prominent types — Clonmacash, Pinar Del Rio, Poweracclaim, Kiss Don't Tell, Ocean Echo, Coincidental Glory, Caislean Ni Cuan and Rosato — will jostle for position in the first two furlongs, creating some early scrimmaging in midfield even if the lead is uncontested. This race shape strongly favours close-tracking prominent runners who can sit just off the controlled pace and produce their effort from 2f out, rather than genuine hold-up horses needing a strong gallop to close into. Several runners tagged REDISTRIBUTED — including Cashel Blue, Absoluteassignment, Beat The Devil, Are You In Or Out and Battleforsupremacy — are true hold-up types forced into a midfield position on the map because the field holds more off-the-pace horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; of these, Cashel Blue and Absoluteassignment are most likely to secure a forward-enough berth given their natural tactical speed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Glasarmi Dictates, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Glasarmi sets a controlled solo lead and the prominent trackers sit close enough to pounce at the 2f pole.
scenarios.body: Glasarmi's uncontested tempo keeps fractions honest and creates a target that close-tracking prominent types can reel in smoothly off the turn; horses like Poweracclaim, Clonmacash and Coincidental Glory, comfortable just off the pace on Good ground, are ideally positioned to accelerate first.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage, Midfield Striker
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack creates enough early pushing and scrapping that a horse sitting just off the melee in midfield finds cleaner air and picks them off late.
scenarios.body: The first two furlongs become busy as Clonmacash, Pinar Del Rio, Kiss Don't Tell and others all try to claim their natural ground, burning slightly more energy than the controlled pace suggests; a horse like Mint Man or Hugo's Girl, ridden patiently just behind the leading pack, threads through on the back of a relatively even tempo.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Glasarmi Goes Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Glasarmi, given a solo lead and a sustainable pace, is simply good enough on the day to hold on and run through the line.
scenarios.body: On Good ground at 6f with no pressure, Glasarmi could dictate every fraction and still have enough reserve to find something when challenged inside the final furlong; the moderate gallop plays to Glasarmi's stamina-based profile and leaves the hold-up types without the closing pace they need to reel in a well-rated front-runner.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Overpower Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is hotter than expected through the prominent cluster scrimmaging, allowing genuine hold-up horses to sweep past tired rivals late.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires Glasarmi or the prominent runners to go faster than their natural rhythm suggests, and with so many of the field's hold-up types forced wide or blocked midfield due to redistribution, a late sweep is the least likely outcome; only a hold-up runner securing genuinely clear ground, like Mint Man or Treasured Royal, could realistically benefit.
